extracted.intended_audience: general readers, literary enthusiasts, and those researching the 2018 Nobel Prize in Literature
extracted.subtask_description: A page describing the 2018 Nobel Prize in Literature (awarded to Olga Tokarczuk) and documenting the committee citation, reactions, and commentary that together articulate qualities the Academy and others valued in a Nobel-level literary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nobel citation: narrative imagination with encyclopedic passion
rubrics_metrics.description: "for a narrative imagination that with encyclopedic passion represents the crossing of boundaries as a form of life."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Swedish Academy's stated reason for the award; it emphasizes an expansive, imaginative narrative voice ('narrative imagination'), breadth and depth of knowledge or scope ('encyclopedic passion'), and an interest in boundary-crossing (geographic, cultural, formal or conceptual) treated as a lived mode ('crossing of boundaries as a form of life').

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing novels in a tension between cultural opposites
rubrics_metrics.description: "She constructs her novels in a tension between cultural opposites: nature versus culture, reason versus madness, male versus female, home versus alienation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing works that set up and explore polarities or binaries, using those tensions as a structural and thematic engine of fiction; the page also notes Tokarczuk is 'inspired by maps and a perspective from above' which frames microcosmos as mirror of macrocosmos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical scope and panoramic portrayal of neglected history
rubrics_metrics.description: Her magnum opus... 'The Books of Jacob' (2014), portraying the 18th-century mystic and sect leader Jacob Frank. The work also gives us a remarkably rich panorama of an almost neglected chapter in European history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include ambitious historical reach, deep research or reconstruction, and the capacity to open up overlooked or neglected historical episodes with panoramic narrative sweep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fusion of embodiment and ephemeral unreality; intimate observation and mythological obsession
rubrics_metrics.description: "Her fusion of intensive embodiment and ephemeral unreality, intimate observation and mythological obsession, make her one of our time's most original prose writers, with new ways of viewing reality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing stylistic hybridity that combines physical, sensory detail ('intensive embodiment') with elements of the uncanny or unreal, and pairing close observation with mythic or obsessive thematic concerns; praised as producing originality and new perspectives on reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtuosity of instant portraiture and capturing characters escaping daily life
rubrics_metrics.description: "She is a virtuoso of instant portraiture, capturing characters in the act of escaping daily life. She writes of what no one else does: 'the world's excruciating strangeness'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes acute character observation, the ability to render vivid, immediate portraits, and a focus on unusual or overlooked aspects of existence; originality of subject-matter and perceptiveness are foregrounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature built on tenderness and psychological interiority
rubrics_metrics.description: From Tokarczuk's Nobel lecture: literature is 'built on tenderness toward any being other than ourselves...it is always psychological, because it focuses on the internal reasoning and motives of the characters, reveals their otherwise inaccessible experience to another person, or simply provokes the reader into a psychological interpretation of their conduct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values empathy, ethical openness ('tenderness'), and deep psychological insight—works that render interior lives, motives, and experiences so readers can understand and share another being's fate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature's capacity to respond to information overload and divisive narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Tokarczuk spoke about her belief in the power of literature in a world of information overload and divisive narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion that literary work should help counter fragmentation and polarization—by offering depth, complexity, and humanization in an era of noisy, polarized public discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and new ways of viewing reality ('writes of what no one else does')
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted praise that she 'writes of what no one else does' and offers 'new ways of viewing reality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly values novelty in perspective, subject matter, and form—prizes originality as a core evaluative dimension for high literary honors.
